title: An archived category keeps its greyed row and its mapping
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location is connected to QuickBooks Online and that AccountingHub is not enabled.
  • Have a new No Charge category for this test, category A, mapped to an expense account at the test location.
custom_steps:
1. Archive category A on the categories page.
  2. Open Integrations > QuickBooks.
  3. Open ShopView Accounts.
  4. Pick a different expense account in category A's row.
  5. Click Save.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Category A is archived.

Step 2:

  • The QuickBooks page opens.

Step 3:

  • Category A's row still shows, greyed, with its account.

Step 4:

  • The new account shows.

Step 5:

  • The row is remapped and saved.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11762 (Story 5, QuickBooks Online account mapping)

  • S5-R1: “Integrations > QuickBooks, ShopView Accounts, shows one row per category directly under Cost of Parts (above Cost of Goods (tax)), grouped under the headers "Internal work orders" and "No Charge work orders", each row named after its category and carrying the QuickBooks mark. A category the shop adds appears as a new empty row; an archived category keeps its row, greyed, with its mapping, and the row can still be remapped (a reopened work order still posts to its archived category, S12-E8). Under the rows a note reads "Shop supplies on internal and no-charge work orders are credited to the income account of your Shop supplies item in Products And Services; nothing to map here." Nothing is created in QuickBooks: the picker lists the location's existing expense accounts.”
  • S5-R6: “The per-category mapping follows the per-row model of part categories, not the fixed ShopView Accounts keys: one row per category per location, keyed by the category's stable key. Archiving a category keeps its mapping; Restore brings it back untouched, nothing is mapped again. The rows exist from the release (S1-R13), so the accountant can map before the setting is on (S5-R5).”

From: "Internal Work Orders technical implementation plan", 2026-10-28, last updated 2026-11-10 (revision 5, built on PRD v1.0), sources/TECH-PLAN-Internal-Work-Orders-upload-2026-11-12.md, read 12 Nov 2026

  • Tech plan line 2880 (TP-349): “(accounts stay editable on archived categories, Q40 \u2713)”
